id: typescript-channels-sender-scoped-group-policy-ignores-route-allowlist
title: resolveSenderScopedGroupPolicy called unconditionally, downgrading routed group allowlist policy
summary: The sender-scoped group policy is computed only from the sender allowlist (groupAllowFrom). When
  a route-level group allowlist is configured but the sender allowlist is empty, the helper rewrites the
  effective policy and drops the routed group policy. This can let messages from group routes through
  that should have been restricted, bypassing the intended allowlist enforcement.
cwe:
- CWE-863
severity: medium
confidence: medium
languages:
- typescript

  ref: e64a881ae0fb8af18e451163f4c2d611d60cc8e4
  vulnerable_ref: e64a881ae0fb8af18e451163f4c2d611d60cc8e4^
  patched_ref: e64a881ae0fb8af18e451163f4c2d611d60cc8e4
  repository: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw
rule:
  message: 'resolveSenderScopedGroupPolicy() is assigned directly without first preserving the routed
    group policy when a route/group allowlist is configured and the sender allowlist is empty. Guard with
    a conditional such as `routeAllowlistConfigured && groupAllowFrom.length === 0 ? groupPolicy : resolveSenderScopedGroupPolicy(...)`.

    '
  patterns:
  - pattern: "const $VAR = resolveSenderScopedGroupPolicy({\n  groupPolicy: $GP,\n  groupAllowFrom: $GAF,\n\
      });\n"
  - pattern-not-inside: 'const $VAR = $COND ? $GP : resolveSenderScopedGroupPolicy(...);

      '
